rationale: Three-lens fan-out ran over the combined two-repo diff; a spec and plan were present so acceptance ran too. All ticket acceptance criteria are implemented and tested, but the review surfaced a concrete security issue (agent-authored regex evaluated on user input, both server- and client-side, with no length cap/timeout and an unhandled re.error path) plus several major gaps: missing license headers on new backend files (a repo-enforced blocking gate), the customer feature flag not enforced server-side, response validation wired only into StandardAssistantHandler, and the plan-mandated turn-end test absent. One decision_needed item forces low confidence. The .env secret-leak the blind lens flagged was remediated during review by rewriting the branch to drop .env from the first commit (local dev .env restored as an uncommitted change; rotate the key if it was ever pushed). 12 lower-severity edge findings were triaged to defer/dismiss (unbounded payload size, deep recursion, mixed-surface rendering, duplicate element ids, empty-options choice) and noted for follow-up.

license headers missing on 9 new backend source files (core/interactive.py, agents/tools/interactive/*, service/conversation/interactive_intake.py, and the 5 new test files) and codemie-ui/src/utils/interactive.ts; repo enforces headers via Makefile license target / husky — CI-blocking (CR-003). alembic versions/ is exempt.
agent-authored regex evaluated against user input without length cap or timeout, server (re.fullmatch) and client (new RegExp), plus unhandled re.error -> 500 (CR-001)

findings.title: ReDoS + unhandled re.error via agent-authored regex on user input
findings.problem: validate_response_values compiles validation.regex (authored by the LLM agent, steerable via prompt injection in tool outputs/docs) with Python's backtracking engine and no length cap/timeout; the same string is fed to new RegExp() in InteractiveForm.tsx (buildSchema). A catastrophic pattern like (a+)+$ with a long user value blocks the request worker; an invalid pattern raises re.error (not ValueError), which escapes the ValueError->422 mapping in validate_interactive_intake and returns 500. Python and ECMAScript regex dialects also differ, so a backend-valid pattern can throw in the browser and crash the surface render.
findings.impact: Denial of service (blocked worker / hung tab) and unhandled 500 on user-controlled input; client-side crash of the chat message tree.
findings.recommendation: Cap field value length and pattern length before matching; wrap re.fullmatch in try/except re.error -> ValueError; validate/whitelist patterns or run matching with a timeout; wrap new RegExp in try/catch and skip (or reject) an uncompilable pattern on the client.

findings.title: Non-ValueError exceptions in validate_response_values reach the client as 500
findings.problem: validate_response_values assumes payload['selected'] is a list and payload['values'] is a dict, and does not type-check payload shape. A non-list 'selected' (int -> TypeError) or a non-dict 'values' escapes as an exception type other than ValueError, which validate_interactive_intake does not map to 422. Combined with CR-001's re.error, several user-controlled inputs surface as 500 instead of a clean 422.
findings.impact: User-controlled payloads produce unhandled 500s instead of validation errors.
findings.recommendation: Type-check payload fields (selected is list[str], values is dict) up front and raise ValueError on mismatch; broaden the intake except to also translate re.error/TypeError to 422, or validate InteractiveResponse.payload with a typed model per kind.

findings.title: Missing license headers on new source files (CI-blocking)
findings.problem: The repo enforces Apache license headers (backend Makefile 'license' target running scripts/license_headers/check_license_headers.py; frontend husky check). Nine new backend files (core/interactive.py, agents/tools/interactive/__init__.py, agents/tools/interactive/request_user_input.py, service/conversation/interactive_intake.py, and the five new test files) and codemie-ui/src/utils/interactive.ts have no header. alembic versions/ is exempt.
findings.impact: CI license gate fails; MR is not mergeable.
findings.recommendation: Run `make license` (backend) and the frontend header fixer over the new files, then amend/commit.

findings.title: features:interactiveElements customer flag not enforced server-side
findings.problem: The 'Disabled features are removed from the catalog' AC and spec section 2 (deployment gate) require the platform flag to gate the feature end-to-end, but _append_request_user_input_tool_if_enabled and the system-prompt injection key only on the per-assistant interactive_features config. The FE hides the form section behind the flag, yet a direct API POST setting interactive_features registers request_user_input on deployments where features:interactiveElements is off. Contrast: hedging checks customer_config.is_feature_enabled('requestHedging') in assistant_handlers.
findings.impact: Platform kill-switch is UI-only; the feature stays active on the backend when disabled.
findings.recommendation: Gate tool registration and the prompt section on customer_config.is_feature_enabled('interactiveElements') in addition to the per-assistant config; add the Helm ConfigMap note per spec section 2.

findings.title: interactive_response validated only in StandardAssistantHandler
findings.problem: interactive_response lives on the shared AssistantChatRequest, but _validate_interactive_response is called only from StandardAssistantHandler.process_request. Other handlers consuming the same model (A2A, background, IDE) accept the field with no request_id/duplicate/value re-validation, and conversation_service persists request.interactive_response unconditionally.
findings.impact: Unknown/duplicate/invalid structured responses can be persisted and replayed to the LLM through non-standard handlers.
findings.recommendation: Decision: either move validation into a shared pre-generation hook that every handler runs, or explicitly scope interactive input to the standard chat handler (and reject the field elsewhere). For a flag-gated v1 the latter may be acceptable — needs a call.

findings.title: Plan-mandated turn-end verification test is missing
findings.problem: Plan B4 named return_direct honoring in the agent loop 'the single most uncertain integration point' and required tests/codemie/agents/test_assistant_agent/test_interactive_turn_end.py asserting no second LLM invocation after request_user_input. The turn-based pause AC rests entirely on the framework's return_direct handling but no test in the diff exercises it.
findings.impact: The core pause/resume behavior is unverified; a langgraph upgrade or config change could silently break it.
findings.recommendation: Add the turn-end test: mock the LLM to call request_user_input and assert the agent stops (no second LLM call) with the interactive_request chunk emitted.
